The Belleek Castle Experience
Here amongst the thumping landscapes of County Mayo, every dream awaits.
For Belleek Castle weddings your fairytale is about to unfold. For countryside escapes, weekend breaks and corporate or private hire, the unforgettable is here for you. Ireland’s most romantic terrain is the destination for your authentic wedding, break or event.
Encircled by majestic woodland, fragrant with ancient Norway Spruce, Scots’ Pine, beech and ash, you’ll find yourself in the most serene setting by the River Moy. Beyond lie endless green valleys, finishing in the beautiful bays of County Mayo’s unspoilt coastline. Soft sands edged by rugged clifftops and Jurassic rock stacks are home to fascinating history, pretty stone villages, waterfalls, top Mayo attractions and magnificent wildlife.
However long your stay with us, it’s guaranteed to be magic.

Castle Hotel Accommodation
Ireland’s Most Original Castle Hotel
Castle Accommodation, Mayo
Our Rooms Are Unforgettable
Four-poster beds and sumptuous furnishings ensure you live out every castle dream. Spacious rooms with large mullioned windows, four-poster beds for most and exquisite period furniture are the perfect place to unwind at any time of the day.
Book a Manor Room and enjoy a four poster bed, additional window seats, extra space and glorious views across Belleek Forest and rural Ballina beyond. Accompanied by queen or king beds, they’re the ultimate retreat.
VIEW ROOMS & Make a booking
Your Tranquil Retreat
Unforgettable Stays In An Epic Irish Setting
Whether you rest your head in a comfy double, queen or king, a wonderful night’s sleep is guaranteed in our tranquil countryside retreat. Sensational four-poster beds made from solid wood are a majestic feature of each room. From intricately decorated wood-panelled headboards to luxe furnishings, you’ll have a sublime place to reside as the sun goes down.
In keeping with the rest of the castle, elegant period furnishings and antiques create a divine setting. Meanwhile, private bathrooms, plasma televisions, complimentary toiletries and tea and coffee facilities ensure you have all the facilities you want.
VIEW ROOMS & Make a booking
A Dazzling Castle Setting
The Warmest Welcome In
Stunning Surroundings
Dine in our award-winning Library Restaurant or enjoy a delicious afternoon tea in one of our elegant period rooms. Head to the Armada Bar for drinks in unique surroundings. Featuring 17th century solid oak baulks salvaged from galleons of the Spanish Armada which were shipwrecked along the coast, it’s a truly unique space.
Other notable places include the medieval Great Hall, a stunning space complete with magnificent 13th century Norman fireplace, wood-beamed vaulted ceiling, wood-panelled walls and medieval-style chandeliers.
Throughout the castle, decorated vaulted ceilings ,wood-panelled walls, antiques, suits of armour, oil paintings, chandeliers and more make Belleek Castle a sensational stay. Conveniently located for exploration of Mayo’s spellbinding landscape, rich with culture and history, we promise a thrilling break on the West Irish coast.
However long your stay with us, we guarantee it will be extraordinary.

pages.text:
Our Story - Belleek Castle, Ireland
Skip to content
About Belleek Castle
Enchanting Tales From The Wild Atlantic Way
Discover More About Belleek Castle
Capturing The Magic Of
Ireland’s Finest Region
Affectionately known as The Wild Atlantic Way, our magnificent castle hotel captures every ounce of Mayo’s reputation as one of Ireland’s finest regions. Drawing together so many of the elements which make Ireland so special, as you uncover our castle’s charming past, you’ll quickly understand why County Mayo, often called Maritime Country, is the home of Irish culture, history and rousing landscapes.
Our Story
If These Walls Could Talk
Belleek Castle has been a family home for most of its existence. Built between 1825 and 1831 in a spectacular Neo-Gothic style, the castle still leaves a lasting impression as you sweep up the drive.
Designed by the legendary Irish Victorian architect, John Benjamin Keanes, the architectural features and period décor present across the castle’s manor house are sublime. From turrets to stone columns, ornate vaulted ceilings and intricate wood panelling, the attention to detail is staggering. A luxurious mix of medieval and Victorian features still leave much to be admired.
Noble Beginnings
Prior to 1825, the castle’s original structure is thought to date back to at least the 13th century. Belleek Castle takes its name from a 13th century Tower House Castle which once stood on the banks of the River Moy.
The castle is the ancestral seat of the first Earl of Arran, Sir Arthur Gore and it’s here that the property’s history as Belleek Castle begins. Under the 1662 Act of Settlement the Gore family were gifted 14,000 acres of land in Ballina.
One of Mayo’s most influential families, the Gores expanded the estate over many generations to a whopping 33,000 acres. By this time the Belleek Castle estate stretched all the way to the banks of the Moy Estuary.
When Arthur Gore’s niece, Mary Gore, married Francis Knox in the 1700s, the family adopted the surname of Knox-Gore. Francis Arthur Knox-Gore, Mary and Francis’ grandson, inherited the estate in 1818.
Ballina’s Finest Landmarks
Shortly after his marriage to Sarah, Francis Arthur Knox-Gore commissioned the construction of Belleek Castle. He is also said to have planted around 2 million trees in Belleek Woods where he was laid to rest in 1873. Francis’ grave in the woods is marked by a striking Neo-Gothic monument designed by James Franklin Fuller.
Though Belleek Castle remained in the Knox-Gore family until 1942, rising costs and residences elsewhere meant parts of the original estate were slowly sold off. The challenges posed by the Second World War resulted in the estate being sold in 1942.
Between 1942 and 1961, Belleek Castle changed hands numerous times, passing from the Beckett Family to Mayo County Council.
Welcome To Our Family Home
In 1961, my father, Marshall Doran, decided to purchase the estate. My father was a merchant navy officer. His passion for maritime history is evident in numerous elements of Belleek Castle, most significantly in the staggering Armada Bar.
Featuring huge, 17th century oak baulks from galleons of the Spanish Armada which were shipwrecked along the nearby coast, the Armada Bar adds another layer of local history to the castle’s fascinating narratives.
The Marshall Doran Collection
Indeed, my father’s love of history led to the creation of The Marshall Doran Collection, Belleek Castle’s superb museum which forms part of our castle tour. My father was an avid collector of fossils and medieval armour so the museum contains all sorts of interesting finds.
With the assistance of John Mullen, my father restored Belleek Castle to its former glory, executing much of the work himself.
Today, Belleek Castle remains a family home and top Mayo attraction which we are delighted to share with you.
Castle Tours
Book A Tour Of The Castle
From the castle’s earliest origins to the Knox-Gore family, Marshall Doran, Jurassic fossils, medieval armour and more, join one of our daily tours to unravel the fantastic history of one of Ireland’s best castles.

wikipedia.title: Belleek Castle
wikipedia.extract: Belleek Castle, originally known as Belleek Manor, is a 19th-century manor house in Ballina, County Mayo in Ireland. Now operated as a hotel, the house was built between 1825 and 1831 in a neo-Gothic style. The 10-room hotel has a museum in its basement containing what is reputed to be Grace O'Malley's bed. It also has a collection of fossils and armoury and a bar named for the Spanish Armada in Ireland. Several structures on the site, including the manor house itself, a nearby mausoleum and 19th-century entrance archway, are included in the Record of Protected Structures maintained by Mayo County Council.
